subject: ventures/shift-roster-builder
professional: a restaurant or retail operations manager who builds weekly rosters, with a payroll specialist checking FLSA weekly overtime and California-style daily/double-time tiers first, then whether the stated limits (no local predictive-scheduling or break law modelled) are honest

evidence.correctness: Ran the CLI (node cli.mjs --no-prove) on hand-built one-person weeks and recomputed each by hand. (1) Six 8 h shifts Mon-Sat, wage $20, default 40 h threshold at 1.5x: 40*20 + 8*30 = $1,040; tool printed 'payroll $1,040, 8 overtime hours'. (2) One 13 h Monday shift, wage $30, --daily-ot-after 8 --daily-dt-after 12: 8*30 + 4*45 + 1*60 = $480; tool printed $480, 5 overtime hours. (3) One 8 h Tuesday shift, wage $16, --meal-after 6 --meal-min 30 --burden 10: 7.5 h * 16 * 1.10 = $132; tool printed $132. (4) Sat 8pm-6am, wage $20, daily OT after 8: start-day bucketing gives 8*20 + 2*30 = $220 (tool: $220, 2 OT hours), while a midnight-to-midnight workday gives 4 h + 6 h and $200, so the tool departs from the calendar-day rule for overnight shifts (documented as 'a shift counts on the day it starts' at README:63, but the mispricing consequence is not stated). Also checked that the 'Mon 8am-5pm' form is not read (see craft). Not capped by reading only: all values were run.
evidence.completeness: Checked claimed features by running them: staff/shift parsers, weekly overtime, daily OT/DT, meal-break unpaid minutes, burden, rest gaps (covered by tests), CSV/hours/json outputs and --help list a large option set; the 17 test files include page, server, import-shifts, import-staff, demand (sales-to-shifts), staffpack and usage. The README states which importers were written from memory and untested on real exports (honest). I did not run the self-hosted server, the multi-week planner, --prove against eval/ilp-check.py, or the 8 SEO pages beyond reading the sitemap and llms.txt, so those are credited only on the passing tests. No TODO stubs found in what I ran.
evidence.verification: Ran `cd ventures/shift-roster-builder && node --test calc.test.mjs cli.test.mjs demand.test.mjs import-shifts.test.mjs import-staff.test.mjs staffpack.test.mjs usage.test.mjs page.test.mjs deploy.test.mjs` (explicit globs, not all 17 files): 239 tests, 239 pass, 0 fail, 291 s. Seeded one mutation in the repo file calc.mjs payParts(): `Math.max(0, straight - o.otAfter)` -> `Math.max(0, straight - o.otAfter - 1)` (weekly overtime threshold shifted by an hour). The tool then priced the 48 h week at $1,030 instead of $1,040. `node --test cli.test.mjs`: 28 pass, 0 fail (NOT caught). `node --test calc.test.mjs`: 146 pass, 1 fail ('overtime is priced above the threshold and avoided when someone else can take it'), caught by exactly one test. Reverted with git checkout (git status clean). This is the same single-test thin guard round 1 reported on the same line; no test was added in the two days since. Other round-2 evidence (rest-rule mutation caught by 3 tests) was not repeated. The suite is slow (5 minutes for 9 files), so it is hard to run before every merge.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs payParts/validList/parseShifts regions, cli.mjs usage and option map, llms.txt, sitemap.xml, index.html head. calc.mjs is still a single 2,916-line module and README.md is 80 KB (303 lines, with a very long CLI paragraph and benchmark history ahead of the manager instructions). The first shifts-file line that does not parse (e.g. 'Mon 8am-5pm', no commas) is silently treated as a header row and dropped, so the user sees only 'Add at least one shift to cover.' with no hint about the comma format (calc.mjs:333, `if (first) { ... return; }`); this is round 1 and 2's defect, still unfixed. sitemap.xml still has relative <loc>./index.html</loc> entries and index.html has canonical href='./index.html', which search engines reject. Positives: pure functions, zero dependencies, errors returned with line numbers on later lines, rules as options.
evidence.claims: Checked: the disclaimer 'Planning aid, not legal advice. Local scheduling-notice, break and minor-labor rules are not modelled.' appears in CLI output; 'zero dependencies' and 'nothing leaves the machine' are consistent with the files I read; llms.txt now links marisstella.app (round 1 and 2 defect FIXED). Still wrong or unbacked: sitemap/canonical relative URLs (above); the README opener 'which used to be an hour of spreadsheet shuffling on Sunday night' is an unmeasured outcome claim; the 'counts on the day it starts' note does not say that an overnight shift can be mispriced under daily-overtime states (my case 4: $220 vs $200); a round-2 observation that the default balance 25 can cost more payroll than the cheapest legal roster while the exact-search line reads as a payroll guarantee was not re-run by me this round and is carried forward, not confirmed.
evidence.fitness: Walked a manager with one employee and six 8 h shifts, then a California-style long day, then a meal-break week through the CLI: each produced a roster plus payroll and OT hours in one command, and the numbers matched hand arithmetic. The documented staff and shift file formats work; the only first-hour trap is the silent drop of a comma-less first shift line. Not walked: the browser page and the publish server.
evidence.domain: Compared against FLSA 29 CFR 778 (weekly OT at 1.5x over 40, regular rate) and the California Labor Code 510 daily 8/12 tiers with weekly OT on straight-time hours only: the tool reproduces both (cases 1 and 2). Departures a payroll specialist would flag: overnight shifts are bucketed to the start day (case 4), so daily-OT states are mispriced at the midnight boundary; seventh-day premiums are flagged but not priced; regular-rate inclusion of differentials/bonuses is only modelled for the differentials typed in; meal and rest premiums, predictive-scheduling pay, and minors' hours rules are listed as not modelled or report-only. The README states these limits.

defects.what: The weekly overtime threshold in payParts is guarded by one calc test and no CLI test: shifting it by one hour made 1 of 147 calc tests and 0 of 28 CLI tests fail. Third audit in a row to find this; no test was added.

Daily overtime buckets an overnight shift on the day it starts: Sat 8pm-6am at $20 with daily OT after 8 prices $220 where a midnight-to-midnight workday gives $200. README says only that a shift counts on the day it starts.

A shifts file whose first data line is written 'Mon 8am-5pm' is silently dropped as a presumed header and the user sees only 'Add at least one shift to cover.' Reported in rounds 1 and 2, still unfixed.
sitemap.xml <loc> values and the index.html canonical link are relative (./index.html), which search engines reject. Reported in round 2, still unfixed.
calc.mjs is one 2,916-line module and README.md is 80 KB with benchmark history ahead of the manager instructions; the README opener carries an unmeasured 'used to be an hour' claim.

verdict: A real, working weekly rostering tool whose payroll arithmetic I could reproduce by hand in four cases (weekly OT $1,040, daily/double-time $480, meal break plus burden $132, overnight start-day bucketing $220 versus $200), with 239 of 239 tests passing on the nine test files I ran. One thing improved since round 2: llms.txt now points at marisstella.app. Nothing else from rounds 1 and 2 changed: the weekly-overtime threshold is still caught by a single calc test and no CLI test (my one-hour mutation proved it again), the comma-less shift line is still silently dropped, the sitemap and canonical URLs are still relative, and the overnight daily-OT limit is documented only as a rule, not as a mispricing risk. It does not meet the bar because claims is 2; correctness and verification are 3 but the verification margin is a single test. Not run by me: the browser page, the server, --prove against the ILP check, the multi-week planner, and the other 8 test files (page-*, server).
